checked.claim: First reconsideration, then Appeal Committee, then High Court
checked.evidence: s 48N and s 48Q are alternatives: an application for reconsideration deems any appeal on the same decision withdrawn (s 48Q(3)), and the reconsideration result can itself be appealed (s 48Q(1)(c)). s 48R: appeal to the General Division of the High Court on a point of law or the amount of a financial penalty; complainants can also appeal (s 48R(2)(b)).
checked.replacement: An aggrieved organisation or person, including the complainant, may either apply to the PDPC for reconsideration (s 48N) or appeal to an Appeal Committee of the Data Protection Appeal Panel (s 48Q); a reconsideration decision can itself be appealed, and applying for reconsideration withdraws any pending appeal (s 48Q(3)). Appeal Committee decisions go to the General Division of the High Court on a point of law or on the amount of a financial penalty (s 48R).

checked.claim: 28 days for reconsideration; appeal deadline reported as 28 days but not confirmed
checked.evidence: The Act sets 'the prescribed period' for both (s 48N(4)(a), s 48Q(1)); Chambers 2026 says reconsideration requests or appeals are due within 28 days. The figure is in regulations not fetched.
checked.replacement: The prescribed period, reported as 28 days, for both a reconsideration application (s 48N(4)) and an appeal to the Appeal Panel (s 48Q); the PDPC may extend the reconsideration period in exceptional circumstances (s 48N(5)).

checked.claim: Not confirmed; secondary sources suggest only financial penalty suspended
checked.evidence: s 48N(3) and s 48Q(4): unless the Commission or Appeal Committee decides otherwise, reconsideration or appeal does not suspend the direction or decision, except where it concerns a financial penalty.
checked.replacement: No for directions, yes for penalties: unless the PDPC or the Appeal Committee decides otherwise, a reconsideration application or appeal does not suspend a direction, but one against a financial penalty does (ss 48N(3), 48Q(4)).

checked.evidence: s 48R(4): same further right of appeal as from High Court decisions in its original civil jurisdiction.
